artboards.title: The brief, the three concepts, the recommendation
A · The daily flow — four real days

annotations.text:
OWNER QUESTION (Aug 29): 'How does the user find everything else?'
Answer boards, below Main: the ACCESS MAP shows the three speeds (always-on · one tap · search-first) and accounts for every current Home surface — nothing is deleted, the tab bar and all stacks are untouched, and the hybrid-v2 Tools area survives verbatim one tap down. The DAILY FLOW board shows four real days, including the guilt-free close.

A · THE NEXT RIGHT THING — unanimous №1
One card, chosen by a published priority ladder (resume work > crisis > overdue > reply > due today > clock window > one question > one opportunity > earned calm). Both states shown: a reply day, and the calm card that gives permission to close the app. 'Not today' always states when the item returns. Tools survive one tap down in the everything-else layer.

B · FRONT DESK — 'the app talks'
Waypoint's opener is one true dated sentence composed locally (no API call); chips are the parent's turn; anything typed or spoken goes to the Navigator with Home context. Cards exist only where the parent pinned an artifact the conversation produced. The Shelf keeps the silent path first-class.

C · CASEBOARD — 'the app shows the true state'
Dated facts only on the board; every derivation quarantined in the Findings drawer with disclosed inputs and a Correct-this control. The sensor line is the provenance contract. The audit's veteran personas (Danielle, Aisha, Rosa) asked for exactly this page.
